characters.name: Phillip "Phil" Dunphy
characters.description: Husband of Claire, father of Haley, Alex, and Luke. He's a classicBumbling Dad, trying to be friendly with his kids despite being a big old dork. He often finds Claire's restrictions on his ideas annoying, but knows she means well, and accepts that she's what keeps him from hurting himself too much. Afraid of Clowns: "Fizbo" reveals that he's deeply uncomfortable with clowns, which is caused by how he once accidentally found a dead clown in the woods as a child. Aging Would-Be Hipster: Phil tries to be the "cool" dad to his three kids by staying hip to modern pop culture. He doesn't do very well — he thinks WTF means "why the face" — mostly earning eye rolls from his two older daughters. His youngest son Luke, however, is more impressionable, at least at first. Amazon Chaser: As he stated in one of his private cams, although it seems that it's not just confidence and strength that he's attracted to:Phil:I'll admit it. I'm turned on by powerful women. Michelle Obama, Oprah, Condoleezza Rice, Serena Williams...Wait a minute. Ambiguously Bi:Played for Laughsvia his numerous man-crushes (including Haley's on-off boyfriend Dylan, weatherman Rainer Shine, and various other men), his numerous 'feminine' hobbies, and this little gem of a conversation with Mitchell during a hectic drive to the airport:Phil:Must be a lot easier just living with a guy. Yeah, life would be simpler if I was gay.Mitchell:Do you think you could get in the fast lane?Phil:Oh I couldtotallyget in the fast lane.Mitchell:I meant the road...

characters.name: Claire Dunphy (née Pritchett)
characters.description: Wife of Phil, mother of Haley, Alex, and Luke. She's far more structured than her husband, and is usually the glue that holds the family together. Unless it's one of the days where their insanity has driven her crazy again. 0% Approval Rating: Despite craving approval from her employees almost as desperately as she craves approval from her father, shenevercatches a break from her subordinates, and her attempts to bridge the gap only make things worse. A-Cup Angst: She's not that insecure about her chest size, but it's a gag that she feels inadaquate when compared to the buxom Gloria. In the episode "Dance Dance Revelation" she stuffs her bra so people will pay attention to her and not to Gloria and in the episode "iSpy", one of Haley's photos features Claire enviously looking at Gloria's cleavage (in a recreation of the famous Sophia Loren side-eying Jayne Mansfield snapshot).Gloria:Claire, I didn't come here to steal your thunder. Your thunder is your thunder and my thunder is my thunder.Claire:I know, it's just that[gesturing at Gloria's chest]God gave youso much"thunder". The Alcoholic:Played for Laughs. Claire really likes her wine. When discussing the time Phil proposed, Claire's memory was being in a bad mood because she was on "day two of a St Patrick's day hangover". Antics-Enabling Wife: Claire rarely stands in the way of Phil'sManchildproclivities, be it hismagic act,Homemade Inventions,odd collections, or his "Didn't Think This Through" large purchases/major household decisions, which tends to conflict with her otherwiseControl Freakcharacterization. However, unlike many examples, she is perfectly willing to help fix the situation and numerous episodes have Phil's shenanigans lead to an overall positive outcome that wouldn't have happened had Claire intervened (or, sometimes,despiteher intervention).

characters.name: Haley Marshall (née Dunphy)
characters.description: The eldest child of Phil and Claire. She's less intelligent than Alex, often coasting through life on her good looks, but she has considerable cunning when she puts it to use. She often weasels out of punishment by helping her parents out of whatever new mess they've gotten themselves into. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Deconstructed. At first it was downplayed, as she was romantically involved withDylan. But after they broke up, she began dating actual jerks who didn't treat her with respect. Finally, after getting sick of it, she started to invert the trope. Ambiguously Bi: Although she has never had a female partner before, once while on vacation she said that whoever they find on the island, weather it was a guy or lady, she’d be kissing it. She also seemingly flirted with homeless car thief Joan. Sarah Hyland had long supported the theory that Haley was truly bisexual and played her with that in mind. Bad Influencer: Subverted. At one point, Haley becomes a social media influencer and is hired to promote nightclubs. Phil disapproves of this and tries to steer her towards a more practical career. However, she demonstrates her skill as an influencer to her dad by using social media to sell a house he was having trouble getting people to buy. Basement Dweller: After getting expelled from college. Phil even warns Luke that he needs to apply himself, because they only have the one basement.

characters.name: Alexandra "Alex" Dunphy
characters.description: Middle child of Phil and Claire, and smarter than the rest of her family. She is a geek, studying hard to get into college and get a good job. Her parents are largely unaware of what she's doing at all times, since they trust she can handle everything herself. Afraid of Blood: AlexFaintingat the sight of blood is a bit of aRunning Gag. It gets to the point where, in the episode Heart Broken," a peeved Claire doesn't even bother to turn around when Alex faints; her only reaction is just an annoyed "Haley, revive your sister." Allegedly Dateless: She has many boyfriends and admirers, but often, her family acts like she's always alone and never gets any dates. Butt-Monkey: Perhaps to offset her snobbery about feeling smarter than everyone, she's often this. Notable examples include her humiliating herself trying to get a picture of Haley doing community service, the entire episode where the rest of the Dunphys try to get her to leave the house for the summer because they think she's bad luck, and the episode where Phil and Claire assume she's making up her boyfriends. Character Development: Throughout the show, she has shown her vulnerable side, showing that she too has struggles and hard times, like that of her siblings. Additionally, her once rocky relationship with Haley has immensely developed, with them being able to confide in each other sincerely.

characters.name: Lucas "Luke" Dunphy
characters.description: The youngest child of Phil and Claire, and a majorCloudcuckooLander, though his weirdness often makes him clever in unexpected ways. Ambiguously Bi: He seems really into Alex's chef boyfriend, and in one episode, he agrees to "hang out and see where it goes" with a man without really putting up a fight. Big Brother Instinct: He's Alex's younger brother, but in one episode he decides to stay with her after she has a bad breakup instead of going to a party. Big Little Brother: In the later seasons, he becomes significantly taller than Haley and Alex. Character Development: While still a bit ditzy, he gained a more prominent mischievous streak after becoming a teenager

characters.name: Dylan Marshall
characters.description: Haley's on-and-off boyfriend-turned husband. A nice boy and honest to a fault, he was more than happy to treat the Dunphys as his own family. He's also slightly dumber than dirt. Abusive Parents:Implied. In one episode, when he (temporarily) lives with Cam and Mitch, he mentions that his mother made him leave because of her new boyfriend moving in. Advertised Extra: Despite his actor gettingPromoted to Opening Titles, he actually appears in fewer episodes than he did in Season 10, only appearing in roughly half of the season. That being said, Dylan overall has appeared in more episodes than any other recurring character in the series. Butt-Monkey: He's a doofus with little understanding of...anything, really, so he's very prone to ending up in bizarre situations like locking himself in the Dunphy's house over their holiday. Cloudcuckoolander: Even surpassing Phil - the kid has no understanding of how normal people act. In his first major episode, he performed a song about how much he wanted to have sex with Hayley. To Hayley's family. While trying to convince them to let her go on vacation with him.

characters.name: Jay Pritchett
characters.description: Husband of Gloria, father of Claire, Mitchell, and Joe, and stepfather to Manny. He is a closet salesman who still owns the company, with a very old way of doing things. He still has a sensitive side, and loves his family deeply. Amicable Exes: Played with. When they have to interact Jay and his ex-wifeDeDeare usually quite civil and pleasant with each other, and any lingering resentments from their marriage appear to be in the past (at least on his part; she's not entirely above bringing up old grievances when it serves her purposes). But he is nevertheless frustrated with her flightiness and selfishness, and it’s made clear they broke up for very good reasons. Brutal Honesty: Jay is honest to a fault. Casting Gag: He is essentially a mirror-universe counterpart to Ed O'Neill'sother famous sitcom role. Where Al Bundy is a slovenly, burned-out loser enduring a hellish lower-middle-class existence trapped in an unsatisfying and degrading marriage, family and working life where he remains forever stuck reliving his high-schoolGlory Days, Jay Pritchard is a wealthy and successful businessman, happily married to a beautiful woman, and while he's not the perfect father he is nevertheless a devoted and rock-solid patriarch to a clan of diverse, close-knit and for all their flaws ultimately loving family members. This even extends to their jobs: both are employed in selling rather functional everyday items, but Al resents and loathes his demeaning job selling women’s shoes, whereas Jay is incredibly passionate (even overly so) about selling closets. Cool Old Guy: In his later years, but still incredibly sharp, witty, and charming.

characters.name: Gloria Ramirez Delgado Pritchett
characters.description: Wife of Jay, mother of Manny and Joe. Gloria is a Colombian national who worked hard for years to provide for her son. She can be eccentric and airheaded at times (not helped by her still-imperfect grasp of English), but she cares for her friends and family above all else. Adoptive Peer Parent: To her step-children, Claire and Mitchell. She is actually younger than Claire, as a few characters love to remind Claire. All Girls Want Bad Boys:Deconstructed. She was once very attracted to the unpredictable Javier, her now ex-husband. But, after having Manny, she realized she needed someone who would be more reliable and not leave her and Manny, especially the latter, hanging on empty promises. Ambiguous Criminal History: She has supposedly been deported twice and is hinted to have worked with her father in a cartel. Attention Whore: This flamboyant woman very much enjoys the limelight, as she makes effort to be noticeable especially when it comes to her appearance and tends to get jealous when other women get more attention than her.

characters.name: Manuel "Manny" Delgado
characters.description: Son of Gloria, step-son of Jay. He's an excessively serious and emotional child who Jay claims was born at least sixteen years old. He and Jay get along well in the way of two old guys, though Jay often tries to make him just act like a kid while he can. Adorably Precocious Child: He's incredibly intellectual and sophisticated for a ten year old. Admittedly, the "precocious" part does bother the adults and doesn't earn him a ton of friends. Berserk Button: The normally level-headed and mature Manny takes another guy’s cell phone and breaks it when said guy insulted a particular film that Manny holds dear to his heart:Mary Poppins. This wasafterwarning Jay that it’s not worth it to give into anger, but is quick to drop this after overhearing another guy degraded Mary Poppins. Big Brother Instinct: Lectures his parents on not arguing will cause harm to Joe, when Gloria is still pregnant with him. After Joe is born, Manny didn't like how Claire was drinking while watching his baby brother and stated as such. Camp Straight: Manny isThe Dandy, a cultured sophisticate and openly emotional, and also has hit on basically every female character he's come into contact with. He's fullyMistaken for Gayin one episode, with Cam and Mitch wondering if he's going through the same thing they did.

characters.name: Fulgencio Joseph "Joe" Pritchett
characters.description: Son of Jay and Gloria. The Baby of the Bunch: The youngest of the titular family,at least until season 11 which brings in three newborns (Poppy, George and Rex). Dead Guy Junior: He is named after his late maternal grandfather. First-Name Ultimatum: By the time he can speak, people don't usually call him "Fulgencio" unless they're scolding him. Generation Xerox: There are numerous instances in which Joe comes off as miniature version of Jay, and more than one subplot addresses this.

characters.name: Mitchell "Mitch" Pritchett
characters.description: Husband of Cam, brother of Claire, father of Lily. Mitchell is a serious lawyer, often exasperated with managing the eccentricities of his husband. All Gays Love Theatre: Never forgave his father for not letting him name his childhood pet bird "Fly-za Minnelli," which Gloria asserts makes it unbelievable that Jay never clocked he was gay. The camera also focuses on Mitch and Cam together during Alex's speech when she mentions people who were drama geeks in high school. Badass Bookworm: Mitchell is a lawyer and has used it to get a boy to confess for taking credit from Manny's work. Closet Geek: He is a huge fan ofSpider-Man's comics, andThe X-Files, but initially the only person aware of these interests in his husband Cameron. In a later episode, he goes for the first time to a science fiction convention withProud to Be a GeekPhil. The Comically Serious: Mitchell quite often, as his serious, uptight personality is contrasted by Cam's more free-spirited, dramatic tendencies.

characters.name: Cameron "Cam" Tucker
characters.description: Husband of Mitchell, father of Lily. He is far more emotional and dramatic than Mitchell, and repeatedly tries to break into stage acting. Also, he used to be a clown. As in from the circus. Action Dad: Despite Cameron being overly dramatic and somewhat effeminate, when he thinks there's a stranger in Baby Lily's room he jumps out of bed, grabs a baseball bat, and charges in with aPre-Asskicking One-Liner.In one episode, when he thought there was a stranger in Lily's room, he jumped out of bed, grabbed a bat, said "It's go time" with aSerious Businesslook on his face, and charged in ready to KILL whoever was in there (fortunately, no one was). In another episode, when Mitch almost gets into a fight with a rudeJerkassat a gas station, Cam gets out of the car and tells the guy he will "slam [his] head into that bumper so hard theairbag will deploy" if he didn't apologize. The guy apologized with genuine fear in his eyes. (Also, Cam was dressed up as Fizbo the clown during this scene, which just makes it more awesome somehow.)In one episode, he gets so pissed off over his extended family being good friends with Mitchell's ex, Teddy, that he punches a punching bag arcade game hard enough to set a record. In one episode, when he thought there was a stranger in Lily's room, he jumped out of bed, grabbed a bat, said "It's go time" with aSerious Businesslook on his face, and charged in ready to KILL whoever was in there (fortunately, no one was). In another episode, when Mitch almost gets into a fight with a rudeJerkassat a gas station, Cam gets out of the car and tells the guy he will "slam [his] head into that bumper so hard theairbag will deploy" if he didn't apologize. The guy apologized with genuine fear in his eyes. (Also, Cam was dressed up as Fizbo the clown during this scene, which just makes it more awesome somehow.) In one episode, he gets so pissed off over his extended family being good friends with Mitchell's ex, Teddy, that he punches a punching bag arcade ga

characters.name: Lily Tucker-Pritchett
characters.description: Adopted daughter of Mitchell and Cam. For the first two seasons, Lily is a baby, and thus doesn't have much characterization. In later seasons, she shows clear signs of inheriting the craziness of the rest of the family, such as by stalking her cousin Manny, or snarking at her fathers' newest problems. Asian and Nerdy: It shows up from time to time. Of course her dads can't help commenting on this:Mitchell:Lily, sweetheart, let's get you dressed.Lily:Hey, I've been dressed for an hour. Come on, I can't be late. I'll fall behind.Mitchell:Sometimes I forget to factor in the Asian.Later, she is revealed to have a genius-level IQ.In "Won't You Be Our Neighbor", she was against being transferred to a less strict teacher's class because her previous teacher taught her math. Later, she is revealed to have a genius-level IQ. In "Won't You Be Our Neighbor", she was against being transferred to a less strict teacher's class because her previous teacher taught her math. Berserk Button: For a while, any mention of her potential new adopted sibling. "Kill the baby!"

characters.name: Frank Dunphy
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: He's a truckload of fun. Generation Xerox: It's really blatant how much he has influenced Phil as a father and as a man. Nice Guy: He's very friendly and cheery to mostly everybody. Sudden Sequel Death Syndrome: In his final appearance in the episode “Legacy” he dies at the end of the episode. (Tragically became a meta example a few months later, when Willard himself passed away.)

characters.name: Grace Dunphy
characters.description: Delicate and Sickly: When she dies, it's implied that she had been sick for a while. The Ghost: She never actually appears on screen. Grandparent Favoritism: Alex is very proud of the special connection they shared; it seems Grace saw a lot of herself in her.

characters.name: Farrah Marshall
characters.description: Abusive Parents: Implied early in the series. In one episode, when he (temporarily) lives with Cam and Mitch he mentions that his mother made him leave because of her new boyfriend moving in. The Ghost: She was mentioned by Dylan a couple of times before actually appearing in seasons 10 and 11, where she took a more significant role as Poppy and George's other grandma. Granola Girl: She's a complete hippie. December–December Romance: With Jerry,DeDe's widowed second husband. Claire thinks that Jerry is mostly attracted to Farrah is because she’s too similar toDeDe. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: An obnoxious, invasive hippie with bleach blonde hair and a complex relationship with her kid? Claire is the first topoint outthat's she's basicallyDeDereincarnate and picks up that JerryHas a Type.

characters.name: DeDePritchett
characters.description: Claire and Mitchell's mother and Jay's ex-wife. Abusive Mom: Mostly towards Claire. She’ll constantly embarrass her and prefers to do it in a public setting, but she doesn’t see anything wrong with it. Notable instances include inviting Claire’s ex-boyfriend without her knowledge (who she is now dating), throwing a surprise party to celebrate Claire’s first period, talking about stories of herFormer Teen Rebelyears like there’s no tomorrow, and once told Claire thatshe ate ice cream like a prostitute. She's also one towards Mitch given her constant coddling and manipulating of him. Amicable Exes: Played with; she and Jay are mostly civil towards each other these days, though she clearly holds a lingering grudge for several issues in their marriage which she's not shy about bringing up if it'll serve her purposes. In keeping with her generalIt's All About Meattitude, however, while Jay was far from the perfect husband at the time (which, to his credit, he's increasingly willing to acknowledge) it's made clear that she had her own responsibility for what happened, and tends to unreasonably act like Jay was the one who "traded her in for a younger model"when in fact she was the one who ended the marriage. Arch-Enemy: She sees Gloria as hers as a result of Gloria marrying her ex-husband. Cheated Death, Died Anyway: In "Good Grief" it's explained in an email that she survived an encounter with a pack of starving timber wolves but using a mixture of howls and barks convinced the wolves to search for food elsewhere, was later saved by one of the wolves after ignoring a thin ice sign and falling into the water, offended an Inuit tribe by interrupting a sacred dagger dance, and briefly got swallowed by awhale. In the end she passed away peacefully in her sleep.

characters.name: Donald "Donnie" Pritchett
characters.description: Big Brother Bully: He and Jay have been play-fighting as long as they can remember; as a result, while they love each other, they struggle to open up on anything more complicated. The Disease That Shall Not Be Named: He refused to tell Jay that he was under treatment for prostate cancer.

characters.name: Becky Pritchett
characters.description: Amnesia Episode: During her first and only on-screen appearance, she is recovering from a stroke that has jammed her memories.Well, she's pretending, really. Daddy's Girl: Implied, as mentioned in the Season 2 episode “The Kiss” that one time her father had kissed Jay goodnight, but instead said “Goodnight, Becky” and in her only appearance Jay said his father had a fishing cabin that he promised would go to Jay, but instead left it to Becky. Evil Aunt: She is so mean that she actually scared the bejesus out of Claire and Mitchell, her niece and nephew, in the past. Grumpy Old Woman: She's harsh and bitter; no one on Jay's side of the family likes her much. Hate Sink: She is not exactly a pleasant person to be around since she is a monster and also demonstrated by her selfish behaviour, she tries to keep Claire’s necklace.

characters.name: Javier Delgado
characters.description: All Girls Want Bad Boys: Deconstructed. Gloria was initially very attracted to him for this, but she eventually divorced him over his inability to grow into the husband/father his family needed him to be. Depending on the Writer: How much of a deadbeat jerk he is depends on the episode. Disneyland Dad: Likes to spoil Manny on the rare occasions he's around, but fails to even be the literal example of this trope in Season 1. He genuinely loves his son; he's just too self-centered and immature to actually be around. So Proud of You: In spite of coming late for Manny's high school graduation, he express to Gloria of how proud he is for raising their son into being such a great young man. This convinces a reluctant Gloria to not chew him out. Visit by Divorced Dad: Goes to visit Manny whenever he visits California.

characters.name: Sonia Ramirez
characters.description: Daddy's Girl: Was apparently their father's favorite, much to Gloria's dismay. Their shared attraction towards Jay is heavily influenced by this fact. Freudian Excuse: Her mother treats her like a maid and refuses to allow anyone to help her, she apparently doesn’t have her own life by the time she visits America for Joe’s baptism, Gloria secretly stole a American job opportunity from her into order to leave their village, and she’s utterly furious to find out that if Gloria hadn’t stolen that opportunity from her, thenshecould have married Jay. Suffice to say that all of this culminated into turning her into a bitter person who resents Gloria. Foil: To her sister. At first, she's aShrinking Violetwho couldn't get a grasp of confidence if it smacked her in the face, unlike Gloria who's a bundle of energy and class... because she's repeatedly stolen opportunities from her. After Sonia realizes this, she comes out of her shell and becomes, unlike Gloria, a genuineGold Diggerrunning after every guy in a semi-fancy suit. The Glorious War of Sisterly Rivalry: Becomes much more apparent after she realizes how many times Gloria snatched opportunities from her, after which she repeatedly attempts to seduce Jay and imitate her sister's life. Pet the Dog: For all her weird antics, she seems to be the only one in Gloria's massive Colombian family that Jay actually likes.

characters.name: Pilar Ramirez
characters.description: Abusive Parent: To both of her daughters. She treats Sonia like a maid, constantly berates Gloria, and guilt-trips both of them into staying at her beck and call. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Around others, she’s a meek old lady, but in front of Jay, she shows herself to be a bitter person that doesn’t like him for the littlest reasons (even bringing out a gun to emphasize it). Jay eventually reveals her true self towards Gloria and calls her out on pretending to be helpless. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: FollowingElizabeth Peña's death, the only appearances of Pena were in episodes that had already been produced, after that, she is never mentioned again. The only reason it can be assumed that she's still alive is that it's unlikely that her death would go completely un-commented on. My Beloved Smother: Right after Gloria has her second baby, she comes over to take full control of managing the baptism for the latter’s son and essentially forces her way into naming the baby after her late husband, even though Jay and Gloria already settled on another name. Jay comes to a compromise to go with “Fulgencio Joseph”, but whispers to Gloria they’ll never call their son by his first name. At one point she expects Manny’s future career as a priest, but Jay puts a stop to that by pointing out he’s a romantic. She’ll often resort to guilt-tripping both of her daughters into doing whatever she wants while acting vulnerable. Obnoxious In-Laws: She really dislikes Jay and doesn't bother to hide it. She’ll subtly threaten him with her gun while remaking all the reason she hates him, such as taking away her daughter, to sending a stranger with a cardboard sign to pick her up at the airport. Jay resorts to using Manny as aHuman Shieldin case she shoots him, to which she doesn’t, but pops a piece of bubble wrap to scare him.

characters.name: Barb Tucker
characters.description: Dirty Old Woman: She often hits on Mitchell, even though he’s gay, is in a relationship with Cam, and is young enough to be her son. In-Universe Nickname: Her full name is Barbara. Mama Bear: Cam mentioned how she once rung the neck of a rooster andserved it for dinnerafter it attacked her son. No Sense of Personal Space: Is very touchy-feely with Mitch. Retcon: In aFreeze-Frame Bonus, the newspaper article about Fizbo in the eponymous episode calls her Jammy. She is afterwards known as Barb.

characters.name: Merle Tucker
characters.description: Grumpy Old Man: He's a Deep South red-blooded American man's man; in that, he gets along pretty well with Jay. He loves his son and has his own ways of expressing it, he's just not exactly a fountain of emotions. Secret Other Family: Downplayed, as they never actually had children; but he spent a full year living apart from his wife, with a younger woman, while letting Cam believe that he was serving in the army well into his forties.

characters.name: Pam Tucker
characters.description: Big Sister Bully: She strong-arms her way into everything and is not above manipulating people to get her way; Cam and Mitch agree that between her and Claire, they really have a lot on their hands. Hair-Trigger Temper: She has areallyshort fuse. While she was living with Mitch and Cam, she would flip off and attack her brother over merely saying certain words. This was why Mitch tried to get her to work things out with her ex and move out. In-Universe Nickname: Her full name, weirdly, is Pameron. My Secret Pregnancy: Kept her pregnancy secret until the day of the birth because she wanted to get a job first and was afraid of her little brother's judgment. Prison Episode: She's in prison for most of season 9, having broken her parole by shoplifting.

characters.name: Calhoun Johnson
characters.description: Big Eater: Can allegedly eat a whole chicken even though he only has two teeth. The Big Guy: He's an exceptionally large and strong toddler.noteReyes was five years old at the time Nephewism: Cam and Mitch agree to raise him while his mother is in prison.

characters.name: Sal
characters.description: I Just Want to Have Friends: Apparently Mitch and Cam are her only friends, but after they adopt Lily, she’s put out of focus. She eventually breaks down over her loneliness and worries if they’ll stop being friends, but Mitch and Cam let her know they’ll always be there for her. Plastic Bitch: When she's first introduced, she's proudly showing off her new breast implants. She's also shown to be an emotionally stunted,party-loving alcoholic, andeven gets jealous that Cam and Tucker's daughter Lily is taking attention away from her. Really Gets Around: She always has a different boyfriend and makes out with a bartender during her bachelorette party. After her divorce, she goes right back to juggling men in between her relationship, and convinced one boyfriend he’s the father of her unborn baby (when everyone can easily tell she’s too late in the pregnancy for that to even be possible). Struggling Single Mother: Is this for a while in Season 6 until Mitchell, Cam, Pepper and Ronaldo all promise to be around as father figures to her son. The Teetotaler: Becomes this in Season 6 after having her baby.

characters.name: Pepper Saltzman
characters.description: A gay friend of Cam's and Mitchell's, known for his parties and his name. Adam Westing: His character is basically Nathan Lane, and anExpyof Albert Goldman fromThe Birdcage. Age-Gap Romance: His love story withFunny ForeignerRonaldo. Camp Gay: Even more than Cam.Mitchell: But it said 'No presents, please.'Cam: Say it like Pepper would say it.Mitchell:[beat]Oh. The Dandy: Always impeccably dressed in exaggerated and stylish outfits. He's known for his infamous parties, which always have elaborate themes and require people to wear either costumes or complicated ensembles.

characters.name: Walt Kleezak
characters.description: Dunphy's next door neighbor. Grumpy Old Man: In spades, though he is slightly more personable once you get to know him.Claire: If Hannibal Lecter and Freddy Kruger had a lovechild, he would be afraid of our next door neighbor.Phil: I don't say bad things about people, but Mr. Kleezak is... not a nice person.Claire: Easy, honey. Intergenerational Friendship: With Luke, who befriends him after knocking on his door out of curiosity. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: As grumpy as he is, he is harmless and doesn't hurt kids. He used to be a fireman.

characters.name: Gil Thorpe
characters.description: A rival real-estate agent who constantly harasses Phil. Always Someone Better: To Phil in real estate. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Luke saves his son life by performing a Heimlich maneuver when the Thorpe boy was choking. Gil actually visited the Dunphy house to thank Luke and Phil for it. Evil Counterpart: Or a more jerkass version of Phil. Hate Sink: Whenever he's on screen, he treatsNice GuyPhil like crap.

characters.name: Andy Bailey
characters.description: The babysitter/nanny for Joe. The family quickly takes a liking to him, especially Phil, due to their similar personalities and interests. Develops feelings for and later dates Haley. Big Damn Kiss:With Haley. Breakout Character: Adam Devine delivered such an outstanding performance in his initial 3 episodes that the writers asked him to come back for more episodes over many seasons. Deadpan Snarker: Occasionally. Dogged Nice Guy: Tohis own girlfriend, Beth, who seems at best indifferent to him. ActuallyAvertedwith Haley, in that she's pretty quick to realize she'd be lucky to have him if he weren't with Beth.

characters.name: TheLaFontaines
characters.description: A loud and obnoxious couple who move in next door to the Dunphys with their children Ronnie Jr. and Tammy. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: They're never seen or heard from again after they destroy the pornographic statue with the Dunphys. Everyone Has Standards: Despite making overly crass jokes and inserting sexual innuendo into all of their conversations, theLaFontainesare genuinely disgusted with their mutual neighbors' unseen pornographic statue on their front lawn, with Ronnie in particular complaining that while he may watch adult material on his flatscreen TV or cell phone inside his house, he'd never put something like that on the street for everyone to see. Jerkass: Are loud and obnoxious towards the Dunphys and also being annoying towards them. Took a Level in Kindness: After bonding over the hate of the pornographic statue, they go to dinner with Phil and Claire and they get on well, which ends their rivalry.

characters.name: Earl Chambers
characters.description: Jay’s former business partner and best friend who is now his business rival and worst enemy. Actor Swap: Played by Jon Polito in Season 6 and 7, but was then played by Robert Costanzo in Season 8 after Polito’s death. Evil Is Petty: He only wanted to hire Mitchell just to create an ad that specifically targeted Jay. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: He's to Jay what Gil Thorpe is to Phil. We Used to Be Friends: With Jay. They used to be best friends and ran their own closet business together, but Earl then betrayed Jay and he is now Jay’s worst enemy.

characters.name: Ben
characters.description: A co-worker of Claire and Jay, has feelings for and later dates Alex. Butt-Monkey: Very frequently at his work and with the family. Extreme Doormat: Finds it extremely difficult to stand up for himself, especially to Jay. Nice Guy: He's a genuinely nice guy, who puts others needs before his.

characters.name: Sanjay Patel
characters.description: A boy in the same grade as Alex and also her academic rival. Bollywood Nerd: The only student smart enough to rival Alex, and he's also Indian. Dating What Daddy Hates: His mother in this case. She is the only one out of his and Alex’s parents that doesn’t take kindly to the two kissing. Stock Foreign Name: Both his first name and his last name are often used as stock names for Indian characters. Unseen No More: After being mentioned multiple times beginning from Season 2, he finally appears in Season 6.

characters.name: Desiree
characters.description: A recently divorced woman who temporarily lived in a house near the Dunphys. She seemed to like Phil despite him being a married man. All Women Are Lustful: There's rumors that Desiree is someone whoReally Gets Around, and she appeared to be interested in Phil after he said some nice things about her when they first met. Later on when Phil helps Desiree get back into her house after she locked herself out, it's quite obvious that Desiree wanted him to stay over. Ms. Fanservice: She's introduced in skin-tight running clothes that show off her cleavage. Really Gets Around: Claire mentions how she heard rumors that Desiree already slept with two dads at the nearby school. What Happened to the Mouse?: Despite her temporarily moving into a house near the Dunphys, she doesn't appear in any future episodes.

characters.name: Rachel
characters.description: What Happened to the Mouse?: It is unknown what happened to her after Gloria took Joe back from her offscreen.

characters.name: Ronnie La Fontaine Jr.
characters.description: Put on a Bus: He disappears altogether after his first appearance, and is only mentioned several times.
